gaps.description: Specific anatomical neck retroversion angle (approx 30°) and inclination neck-shaft angle (130°-135°) require quantitative source synthesis.
Physiological range of motion in degrees for flexion, extension, abduction, and internal/external rotation requires secondary source attribution.
Reconcile institutional mention of axillary nerve contribution vs classical subscapular nerve exclusive innervation.
Formal demarcation of anterior boundary (subscapularis superior border), superior boundary (supraspinatus anterior border), and apex (transverse humeral ligament).
Documentation of axillary pouch, subscapular recess, and bicipital tendon synovial sheath extension.
Detailed bony insertion dimensions and facet topography across the superior, middle, and inferior facets of the greater tubercle.
Bifurcation into medial and lateral bands embracing the LH biceps tendon and blending with the fibrous capsule and supraspinatus/subscapularis tendons.
Topographic encircling by the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery within the quadrangular space interface.
In normal anatomy, subacromial-subdeltoid bursa does NOT communicate with glenohumeral joint cavity; communication is pathognomonic of full-thickness supraspinatus tear.
Upper 60% tendinous insertion into lesser tubercle crest vs lower 40% muscular insertion into proximal humeral shaft.
